title: Errors: what is failing, and which fault

options.content:
Two questions, and they are answered by different signals on purpose (ADR-0503).

**How much** is `errors_total{service, kind}` — a bounded metric, five `kind` values, and the only thing here that alerts. **Which fault** is `error.fingerprint`, which is log structured metadata and a span attribute and is *never* a metric or stream label — so it is queried out of the log store below rather than aggregated in Prometheus (ADR-0500's cardinality discipline).

There is no persistent fingerprint store on this floor, so "is this fault new?" is a comparison of two windows rather than a lookup. That catches a new fault within the window and misses one that appeared and stopped inside it — a narrower guarantee than a tracker's, not an equivalent one.

panels.title: Error rate by kind
panels.description: The bounded metric. A shift between kinds is often the story: dependency rising while internal is flat is something else failing, not this service.

panels.title: Error rate by service
panels.description: Unfiltered by the variable above, deliberately: this is the panel that says whether one service is failing or the platform is.

panels.title: Faults in the last hour, by fingerprint
panels.description: Grouped by the computed fingerprint, so one row is one fault however many times it happened. The count is the occurrences; open a row to reach the trace.

panels.title: Fingerprints seen this hour and not the hour before
panels.description: The new-fault check, as a query rather than as state (ADR-0503). A row here is a fault whose first occurrence is inside this window. It is a set difference over two windows, so a fault that appeared and stopped within the previous hour does not show up — that is the accepted gap, not a bug.

targets.expr: sum by (fingerprint) (count_over_time({service_name=~"$service"} | json | fingerprint != "" [1h])) unless sum by (fingerprint) (count_over_time({service_name=~"$service"} | json | fingerprint != "" [1h] offset 1h))

panels.title: Recent error logs
panels.description: The raw stream behind the tables. `fingerprint` is structured metadata here, never a stream label — filtering by it is a line filter, which is why these queries parse rather than select.
